sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Monroe County, Florida?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the work in Monroe County. The property appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and the tax collector mails the bills and takes the money. Florida's Department of Revenue describes the same split for every county, and it is the reason a Key West seller and a Marathon seller call different counters for different problems.

The tax collector's own page says the appraiser's January 1 value, combined with millage rates set by the Board of County Commissioners and the other taxing bodies, produces the tax roll. The roll is certified to the tax collector, who prints and mails the notices to the owner's address of record. If a mortgage company pays through escrow, the lender asks for the bill and the owner receives an informational copy.

The same page tells owners that a missing bill is still the owner's problem. A separate bill goes out for each parcel, matched to the way the deed is recorded, so an owner of two lots should expect two notices.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in the Keys?
sections.html:
Monroe County has few people for its size. QuickFacts shows 80,406 residents for mid-2025, a 3.0 percent dip against 2020, and 983.04 square miles of land, which worked out to 84.3 people per square mile in 2020.

Price and tax planning start with the housing numbers. The five-year survey data gives $780,600 as the median value of an owner-occupied home, with 65.8 percent of units lived in by their owners and 56,009 units counted in 2025. Rent at the median is $1,999 a month. Older residents are 27.2 percent of the county, so the senior and homestead programs below see heavy use.

  • Veterans counted for 2020 to 2024: 5,674, so the veteran exemptions listed further down apply to a real share of owners.
  • Mean commute: 19.5 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 279.

sections.html:

sections.h2: Who lives in Monroe County, and what do they do for work?
sections.html:
The Census profile shows an older, higher-income and international county. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $87,738 in 2024 dollars and per capita income is $59,543, with 10.9 percent of people in poverty. Foreign-born residents are 19.8 percent of the population, and 22.2 percent of people age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home.

Visitor spending shows in the 2022 business numbers: accommodation and food services sales totaled $2,245,213 thousand, and retail sales were $2,157,198 thousand, or $26,430 per resident. In 2023 the county had 4,154 employer establishments and total employment of 37,134, up 5.4 percent from 2022.

  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 38.6 percent.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 89.9 percent.
  • Residents in the same house a year earlier: 84.8 percent.

For a seller, this means a buyer pool that often includes second-home buyers and remote workers, who may pay a different amount in tax than the current owner does.

sections.h2: How should a Keys owner prepare an appeal or a correction?
sections.html:
Start with the August notice of proposed property taxes, which the state says the appraiser mails. A challenge to value is a petition on one of the DR-486 forms, filed with the clerk within 25 days of that notice. Mark that date the day the notice arrives, because the window is short.

An exemption denial runs on a different clock: a petition to the value adjustment board goes in 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. Filing the exemption in the first place is due by March 1, and tangible personal property owners with rental furnishings or business equipment file Form DR-405 by April 1.

  • Gather recent sales of similar properties on your island or key before you file.
  • Photograph any damage that existed on January 1, since value is set on that date.
  • Keep the notice and your filing receipt together.

Ask the property appraiser for the comparable data used on your parcel, and ask the tax collector for a payoff figure before you close.

sections.h2: What is the Monroe County tax calendar for bills and discounts?
sections.html:
Bills go out on or before November 1, and the full amount is due by March 31. Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

  • Pay in November and the discount is 4 percent.
  • December brings 3 percent.
  • January brings 2 percent, and February brings 1 percent.
  • March is the gross amount with no discount.

Florida's revenue department adds that tax certificates are sold on unpaid accounts by June 1. The tax collector's page also points owners to alternative payment options: a quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment plan and a homestead tax deferral program. For the installment plan, the state says to apply by May 1 of the assessment year. Deferral applications go to the tax collector on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Keys sale?
sections.html:
A capped assessment is a benefit tied to the owner, and it ends when the house sells. In a county where the typical owned home is valued at $780,600, the distance between a long-held capped value and a fresh assessment can be wide.

The state's homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value, with the filing deadline on March 1. The cap on yearly growth is the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and the Department of Revenue chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale, the next January 1 assessment starts from just value for the new owner. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which has a three year window.

sections.h2: What other exemptions might a Monroe County owner have?
sections.html:
With 5,674 veterans and a 27.2 percent senior share, Monroe County owners often ask about relief tied to service and age. The state lists a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veterans 65 and older, and a possible total exemption for permanent and total disability.

Seniors may also benefit from an optional local ordinance. Ask the property appraiser whether Monroe County or a city in it has adopted one, and what income limit applies.

sections.h2: How are taxes and deed costs handled when a Keys house closes?
sections.html:
Taxes for the year of sale are normally split between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, and the title company will pay or credit them. Since bills arrive in November for the full calendar year, a seller who closes in the spring or summer has usually not seen that year's bill yet.

A deed in Monroe County carries documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration under section 201.02. Miami-Dade is the one county with a different rate. The state says every party to the document stays liable, whoever agrees to pay, and the clerk takes the payment when the deed is recorded. The clerk's own page fees come from section 28.24: $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each page after, and extra per-page technology and trust fund charges.

If taxes go unpaid, the process runs to a certificate sale and later a tax deed sale handled by the clerk. A certificate holder may apply for a deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the year of issuance. Clear all of it before a closing.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Monroe County property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: Pay by March 31. That is when the gross amount falls due, and April 1 starts delinquency. Earlier payment, November through February, shrinks the bill by 4, 3, 2 or 1 percent.

faqs.q: Which Monroe County office do I call about a missing tax bill?
faqs.a: The tax collector. Its property tax page lists (305) 295-5044 for missing statements, and each parcel gets its own bill according to how the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes cap if I sell my Keys home?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1, so the buyer's assessment starts fresh. Portability may let you carry part of the savings to a new Florida homestead if you file in time.

faqs.q: Can I pay Monroe County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the tax collector's quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment option or a homestead deferral. State guidance says to apply for installments by May 1 of the assessment year.

faqs.q: Who runs a tax deed auction in Monroe County?
faqs.a: The clerk of the circuit court runs the sale. Under Florida law a certificate holder can apply once two years have passed since April 1 of the issuance year, so unpaid taxes should be cleared well before then.
